Great to meet you on the call yesterday. As discussed, I'm starting the contracting thread so we can capture the initial asks and get the right template into legal's queue. Attached are two short things from our side: (1) template_variants.pdf — our standard MSA and a leaner commercial order-form-first variant, and (2) a blank party_sheet.csv to populate counterparty contact and billing details.

Could you please confirm the following so we can map exhibits and hosting/residency requirements:
- Full legal entity name and any DBAs you want on the MSA (as it should appear on the signature page)
- Billing contact, PO process, and whether ProcureOps will require an SOW/work order before signature
- Hosting region preference and any data residency constraints (US only / EU / hybrid)
- Any standard procurement clauses you expect (e.g., 3rd-party indemnity, flow-down terms, specific IP carveouts)

If you have an initial redline, feel free to send it back (docs are fine). We'll triage and return a marked-up with a proposed Exhibit mapping and priority flags. Marissa and Karthik are on the thread for legal intake; Kimberly will coordinate billing and invoicing fields.

Next steps: if you can return the filled party_sheet.csv and any redlines by end-of-day Wednesday (4/14 PT) we’ll aim to get first-pass comments to you by Friday. If that timeline doesn't work, tell us your preferred date.

Thanks —

Thanks David — I pulled the redline and did a quick pass. High-level notes (will produce short recommended positions doc by Friday morning):

1) Indemnity & cap: Opsynchrony's redline proposes a mutual indemnity but moves to a lower cap tied to fees; we should push to keep cap tied to 12 months' fees and preserve carveouts for IP infringement. If they insist on lower, we can trade for stronger warranty carveouts.

2) SLA credits: they request credits for any outage >5 mins. We should clarify critical API endpoints and propose a tiered SLA with thresholds and cumulative monthly caps to avoid open-ended credits.

3) Data segregation: request for explicit vendor-flow-down for analytics partners is reasonable. Recommend adding an Exhibit (Exhibit D) that requires contractually obligated flow-down to named sub-processors — limit scope to customer-provided data types.

Open questions for Opsynchrony (Kimberly / David to ask in reply):
- Do they require SOC2 Type II attestation as standing evidence, or will an onboarding security questionnaire suffice?
- Any preferred signatory? (we need exact name and title for the signature block)

I flagged the redline with comments where we expect pushback. Karthik and I will coordinate on proposed language; I'll call out 3 priority clauses we want commercial to approve trade-offs on.

-marissa

Marissa Cole
